newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo, HK stocks seen well supported this week.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo, HK stocks seen well supported this week.

text.p: Tokyo and Hong Kong markets could be poised to move up this week after both centres ended last week close to key technical levels.
Tokyo was seen rising after the Nikkei breached resistance at 21,406 last week, while Hong Kong could test the 12,000 point level after the Hang Seng hit a 31-month high, brokers said.
Meanwhile, Thai stocks were expected to rebound after Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's decision to call snap general elections to break a deadlock on a choice on his successor.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks are likely to be have a firm tone this week after the Nikkei average rose above resistance at 21,406, the level marked at the end of the last business year in March.

Shunichi Ishimura, general manager of the equity department at Nomura Securities Co Ltd, said sentiment was currently upbeat, with a flow of new money expected to pour into the market from investment trusts in October, and interest rates unlikely to rise in the immediate future.
"I expect the Nikkei average to break above 22,666 by the end of this year," Ishimura said.
On Friday, the key 225-share Nikkei average rose 85.65 points or 0.40 percent to close at 21,547.02 versus 21,112.24 the previous Friday.
HONG KONG - The Hang Seng index is expected to head towards its next target of 12,000 points after closing at a 31-month high on Friday, analysts said.
The blue chip index hit a new 1996 high on Friday at 11,788.41 before closing the session at 11,759.39 points, up 123.26. The index rose 167 points, or 1.44 percent in the week to Friday.

"The momentum may indeed carry over into (this) week. There is an absence of negative factors which should propel increased liquidity with also overseas participation," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"I think breaking 12,000 is possible," he said.

BANGKOK - Thailand's extended bearish stock market should stage a quick and strong rally on Monday in reaction to Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's decision to call snap general elections to break a deadlock on a choice on his successor.

Barry Yates of Multi-Credit Corp of Thailand said the SET Index could rebound at least 100 points over the next few weeks before encountering profit taking at the 1,150-1,200 level. The index ended Friday before the election announcement at 1,047.95.

Analysts said the market got a big psychological boost from Banharn's decision as the opposition Democrat Party, the biggest potential winner of the November 17 polls, stands a good chance of leading the next coalition with a stronger economic team.
JAKARTA - Jakarta share prices are expected to stay firm, with brokers anticipating speculative buying of selected second-liners and market heavyweights.
"Active buying of selected second-liners and market heavyweights is likely to continue due to speculative reasons," one broker with a foreign brokerage firm said.
On Friday, the Jakarta composite index closed at 573.30 points against the previous week's close of 568.99 points.
KARACHI - Pakistani stocks are expected to open mixed due to political unrest when the Karachi bourse reopens after the Friday and Saturday weekend, dealers said.
"Political unrest and violence have dampened the market sentiment, which showed some signs of improvement in the last week," dealer Majid Chapra said.
On Thursday, the Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index closed 1.94 points, or 0.14 percent, down at 1,382.57, compared with the previous week's close of 1,438.42.
KUALA LUMPUR - Dealers and analysts said investors would begin to focus on undervalued Main Board stocks after big gains on the Second Board in recent weeks.
"We are anticipating a run-up in 'pale-blue' (medium-capitalised) stocks," " said John Engle, managing director of brokers HG Asia.
Week-on-week, the Composite Index was down 0.01 points at 1130.59, while the Second Board index fell 11.55 points at 595.58.
MANILA - Overseas markets are expected to influence the Philippine bourse, as investors take their cue from their foreign counterparts, brokers said.
"The Philippines will still take its cue from the bigger markets. Most of the fund managers will still be revaluating their investment strategies," Raph Mondragon of OCBC Securities said.
The 30-share composite index closed lower at 3,223.71 versus the previous Friday's 3,242.22.
SEOUL - Blue chip shares are expected to continue to climb on Monday as domestic investors prepare for the week's expansion of the foreign shareholders' ceiling.
On October 1, foreigners will be able to buy up to 20 percent of most stocks, up from the current 18 percent.

On Wednesday, the composite index closed at 793.21, up 33.86 points or 4.46 percent from last Friday's closing of 759.35. The market was closed from September 26 to September 28 for Chusok, the Korean Thanksgiving holidays.
SINGAPORE - Dealers said Singapore stocks would be mixed and they expect the key Straits Times Industrial index to trade sideways within a tight range between 2,150 to 2,180.

"The market will be drifting in directionless trade. Corporate result season has just ended and the Singapore market seems immune to whatever's happening on Wall Street," said an institutional dealer.
The Straits Times Industrials Index closed at 2,171.05 on Friday, down 16.81 points week on week.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market is expected to extend its recent strong gains in the near term as solid buying interest underpins a buoyant market. The key All Ordinaries index closed the week at 2,283.0, up 42.2 over the week.
While options expiries dominated turnover, brokers said the tone remained firm with the bullish outlook supported by continuing offshore and local investor interest.
"There is no reason why we shouldn't go ahead. Interest rates look stable in the (United) States so we should continue to move ahead," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at broker Intersuisse.
WELLINGTON - Growing political uncertainty in the run-up to New Zealand's October 12 election saw the share market close weaker on Friday, and brokers expected equities to drift lower this week.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended last week at 2222.02, 16.86 points lower week-on-week.
BOMBAY - Shaky Indian shares are expected to drift lower this week as investors stay on the sidelines to await political developments, brokers said.
They expect former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao to be arrested on Monday, when he appears in court in a conspiracy case. Two other accused are in jail pending trial.
Concerns about the impact of Rao's legal troubles on the minority coalition government which relies on his Congress party's support in the house will overshadow trading, dealers said.
The concerns dragged the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange down 92.05 points, or 2.75 percent, to 3,254.73. - - - -
TAIPEI - Taiwan share prices are expected to consolidate in a narrow range in cautious trade as many shares are now at high levels, brokers said.
The stock market was closed Friday and Saturday due to domestic holidays. On Thursday, the index ended at 6,508.17, compared with 6,535.59 the previous Thursday.
A 6,450-6,550 trading range was seen for this week.
